title: Stopping or leaving while OBS auto-configuration is in flight lets configure finish after teardown and leaks a fresh OBS control channel
test: tests/browser/host-obs-control-channel.spec.mjs: 'Stop Sharing while a Retry configures OBS stops OBS once that retry ends, not before it', 'Start Sharing again while the stopped session still configures OBS waits for that setup, whose stop lands first', 'Leave and Stop during OBS setup stops OBS once it ends, and a host view opened again configures OBS only after that stop' (all three failed before); 'a Retry that ends after Stop Sharing opens no control channel' (existing, changed: it pinned the immediate stop). Unit tests: tests/obsOperationQueue.test.js (14 tests: FIFO order, rejections, ownership claim and release, stale stop skipped while a newer live session owns OBS, stop for S before a later configure, teardown of S during configure then Start of S2 with the real start-operation guard)
proof: Holds in part. TASK-063 had already removed the leaked channel and the state updates after teardown (abandonIfStale after the configure, establishObsControlChannel checks the session) and added an unqueued compensating stop for a stale start when no successor owned the session. What was left, shown with a stub obs-websocket (page.routeWebSocket on :4455, one global stream, a held SetStreamServiceSettings, an ordered request log) against a real server.js with WHIP on, on the unchanged client (output in dev-notes/results/TASK-071-before-e2e.txt): (1) Stop during a Retry: Stop's fallback stop went out at once, before the retry's StartStream, and nothing followed, so OBS kept streaming at the ended room (Expected false, Received true after 15 s); the changed existing test shows the same immediate stop (connections opened by Stop: Expected 3, Received 4). (2) Stop during the start's configure, then Start Sharing again at once: the new session configured OBS at the same time as the old setup (2 connections opened while the first setup was held, 'Connecting to OBS...' instead of a wait), the old setup then wrote its target over the new one, and the compensation was skipped because a successor owned the session, so OBS ended streaming to the old room (Expected .../C3AC5B, Received .../59NU5S). (3) Leave and Stop during setup, back to #host and Start again: the same, across the remount (Expected .../WFHTE8, Received .../9S8CC3). Fix: new src/lib/obsOperationQueue.mjs, one module-scope FIFO queue for the page with an ownership record (owner token, changed only inside a running queued operation). Every configureObsStream call (Start and Retry) and every non-unload stop run through it; the token is TASK-063's start-operation id. A configure claims OBS when its turn comes (skipped entirely if its session ended while it waited), and after configureObsStream a stale one sets no state and opens no channel; if the owner is still its session it stops OBS in the same operation (when auto-start was on or the configure succeeded, or when its teardown left the stop to it; never after a reload-preserving pagehide) and releases ownership. A teardown whose session's configure is queued or running sends no stop of its own (deferStopToConfigure; any open channel is closed); otherwise it queues the stop (channel.stopStream then close, or the stopObsStream fallback), which runs unless a newer live session owns OBS and then releases ownership. Only pagehide writes StopStream on the open channel at once, unqueued. A new configure waiting behind another operation shows 'Waiting for the previous OBS setup to finish...'. After the fix all 6 tests of the spec pass (18 of 18 with --repeat-each=3): one StopStream lands after the old setup's last request and before the new setup's first, none after the new stream starts, OBS ends streaming to the new room with its control channel the only open connection; the Retry case ends idle with exactly one stop after the retry's StartStream. Checked with npm run lint, npm run typecheck, npm test (1394/1394) and the whole browser suite (76 passed, 13 skipped as configured).
